newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tietmeyer sees no reason to raise rates.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer sees no reason to raise rates.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday he saw no reason to raise German interest rates but could not say whether there was room to cut them.

In an interview with French television TF1, he also said that high German unemployment was not a monetary problem and the Bundesbank therefore did not have a responsibility to alter rates in order to reduce joblessness.
"We regularly verify if our interest rate policies correspond to monetary policy. For the time being, we have no reason to change rates," he said.
"As to whether there is room to reduce rates, that is a question to which I cannot now respond. We are going to monitor the situation."
A French transcript of the interview to be broadcast on Thursday night was provided by TF1 and was translated into English by Reuters.

Asked whether he had a responsibility to act to reduce unemployment, Tietmeyer said the bank's responsibility was "to create good financial conditions for investments and to offer savers the possibility of getting appropriate interest."
"Our interest rates are now at historically low levels, both long and short-term," he said. "And all German investors agree that monetary and financial conditions are as favourable as ever."
He said he believed Germany's high unemployment was due to a "too many rigidities" affecting new investments and the labour market itself.
"Then you must add in that our labour costs, and especially fees, are too high. Everyone is in agreement on that judgment," he said.
He said another problem with the German labour market was that there was "too much insecurity" in salaries, financial conditions and workplace regulation.
"In Germany, everyone agrees that there is no conflict between monetary policy and bringing down unemployment," he said.
Tietmeyer also said that public deficits and public finances must be kept under control, "which means that spending must grow more slowly and that, on the other hand, charges must be reduced.
